MSFT.reasoning: Well, I’m looking at Microsoft, and I’m seeing a classic tale of a wonderful business at a price I can’t quite figure out. The numbers on the growth side are incredible – revenue up 32.9% and earnings per share skyrocketing 40.9%. That’s the kind of expansion that gets me excited, the sort of story where you wish you could hop in a time machine and buy it five years ago. The fundamentals are rock-solid, too: debt is tiny relative to equity, operating margins are a dreamy 44.7%, and they’re generating more free cash flow than most companies could dream of. Plus, I see insiders are buying more than they’re selling – 33 buys to 16 sells – that’s a nice little vote of confidence from the folks in the know. But here’s the rub: I can’t find any valuation data. No PEG ratio to tell me if I’m paying a fair price for that growth. Without the price tag, it’s like walking into a store and knowing you love the product but having no clue if it’s on sale or marked up 300%. My kids use Windows and Office, and I’ve seen how Microsoft products are everywhere – it’s a ten-bagger in its past, no doubt. But at this size, expecting another ten-bagger is like casting a net in a pond you’ve already fished dry. So, I’m stuck in neutral. It’s a great company, but without the PEG, I can’t call it a GARP play. I’m not selling it; I’m just not buying more until I see the sticker price.
